answer: Charge a work-bonded admission: before an agent can settle on the open book, it must lock a walnut of fees it itself earned, then survive one juniper cycle in which only counterparties with uncorrelated histories may countersign its jobs. Those signatures are hashed into a single pigment bound one-to-one with the locked stake. A farm of aliases cannot split one walnut, cannot reuse another agent's pigment, and cannot recruit correlated signers without the seals being rejected. Cheap identity multiplication therefore fails at both cost and uniqueness.
